children: At a roundtable with executives from Micron, Intel, AMD, ASML and other semiconductor majors, the prime minister called for greater industry participation in skilling, innovation and emerging technologies as India moves from building the foundations of its chip ecosystem to scaling up

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called on global and Indian semiconductor companies to play a larger role in the next phase of India's chip-sector development, as New Delhi seeks to expand the ecosystem beyond initial manufacturing projects into research, advanced technologies, talent and supporting industries.

Modi made the call at a semiconductor CEO roundtable at Seva Teerth in New Delhi. The meeting brought together senior executives from companies including Micron, Intel, AMD, ASML, Infineon, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, Tata Electronics, Lam Research, NXP, Foxconn and CG Power.

The prime minister said India's semiconductor ecosystem was moving from a foundational phase towards one of greater scale and opportunity, according to a government statement. He urged companies to participate not only in manufacturing but also in skilling, innovation and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing.

Modi also reiterated the government's commitment to providing what it described as a predictable and responsive policy environment for the industry. At the same time, he said policy would need to evolve with technological changes and industry requirements.

He invited semiconductor companies to provide suggestions on policy and administrative measures, saying their inputs would be considered as the government works to strengthen the sector. The prime minister also referred to India's target of training one crore people in AI and said the country's talent pool, combined with the capabilities of global technology companies, could create opportunities in emerging areas.

The government has been seeking to deepen India's semiconductor capabilities after the first phase of its semiconductor programme approved projects spanning fabrication, assembly and testing, chip design and other parts of the ecosystem. SEMI said ahead of the 2026 event that three of the 12 projects approved under the Semicon India Programme had already begun commercial production.

Industry representatives at the roundtable said the progress in manufacturing, design, infrastructure and talent had created a foundation for further participation. They expressed confidence in opportunities under the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission and in India's ability to develop capabilities across manufacturing, R&D, advanced technologies and supporting industries, the government said.

The participants included representatives from SEMI, Micron, Infineon, Applied Materials, ASML, Merck, Tokyo Electron, Fujifilm, AMD, Intel, Tata Electronics, Lam Research, Rapidus, NXP, Foxconn, Semiconductor Devices, Advantest, Celesta Capital, CG Power and IBM Research, among others.
